prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1123; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment kept growing well beyond what this injury usually needs, with more visits and new services added month after month.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a parking lot collision with a reported neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report and the statements from two witnesses, who both describe the other vehicle backing into the claimant's car at low speed. The other driver's account matches theirs.

Entry 3: Photos submitted by the claimant and the body shop show damage to the rear bumper and tailgate that lines up with the impact described. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from prior claims or repair records.

Entry 4: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the coverage was active on the day of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who provided the initial medical report describing neck and back strain. The reported injury is consistent with a collision of this type.

Entry 6: The claimant has given the same account of the accident in every conversation so far, including the recorded statement and the follow-up call. The details have not shifted.

Entry 7: Reviewed the claimant's prior insurance and medical history. No earlier injury to the neck or back has been identified in the records provided.

Entry 8: Treatment has grown steadily over the past months, with additional visits and new services added each month. The volume now runs well beyond what is typical for a strain of this kind, and I have requested the treatment records for review.

Entry 9: Police and witness statements confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision, which is consistent with the medical timeline provided by the attorney.

Entry 10: File remains open pending receipt of the complete treatment records and a review of the billing against the injury. Next step is to schedule an independent medical review.
